answer: In LINE’s first-order proximity model, the joint probability of an undirected edge between nodes i and j is defined with a sigmoid over the dot product of their embeddings: p1(i,j) = 1 / (1 + exp(-u_i^T u_j)). The empirical probability in this setting is based on the observed edge weight w_ij normalized by the total edge weight in the graph: \hat{p}_1(i,j) = w_ij / W, where W = \sum_{(i,j) \in E} w_ij.
confidence_reasoning: This matches the standard LINE formulation for first-order proximity and the empirical edge distribution used in the paper.
